candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 34:11 (Joseph sold and annual fast (34:11)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And they sat down to eat bread, and they sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of gold; and they brought him down into Egypt, and they sold him to Potiphar the eunuch the chief cook of Pharaoh' — Jubilees follows the Gen 37 sale of Joseph with a notable detail (twenty pieces of gold; sold to the Ishmaelites). Tewahedo Holy-Week typology preserves the canonical Joseph-as-Christ correspondence: sold for twenty pieces of gold (cf. Mt 26:15 thirty pieces of silver for Christ — the parallel-but-distinct sums anchor the doubled betrayal motif). Tewahedo liturgical commemoration of the Joseph-betrayal date on Wednesday of Holy Week draws on this canonical typological pattern.

candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 34:18 (Joseph sold and annual fast (34:18)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'For this reason it is ordained for the children of Israel that they should afflict themselves on the tenth of the seventh month — on the day that the news which made him weep for Joseph came to Jacob his father — that they should make atonement for themselves thereon with a young goat on the tenth of the seventh month, once a year, for their sins; for they had grieved the affection of their father regarding Joseph his son' — Jubilees uniquely connects the Day of Atonement (10th of 7th month, Lev 16) to the day on which Jacob received the news of Joseph's loss. The Tewahedo Day of Atonement (Astereyo) is canonically anchored TRIPLY in Jubilees: the Watchers judgment (Jub 5:17-18), the Noahide atonement pattern (Jub 6 indirectly), AND now Jacob's Joseph-grief (Jub 34:18). The Tewahedo's distinctive emphasis on grief-of-affection (not just sin-against-commandment) as the canonical heart of Atonement Day finds anchor here.
